summary:
You finish at twenty past eleven.
It is done, it is merged,
So you open the next thing,
Two hours later
That break cost you the afternoon.

The price is zero.
Twenty minutes into the next thing
An hour in, it is the hour,
And the price keeps rising
We choose breaks by feel.
Feeling is a terrible clock.
It reports fatigue late,
So take them at the seams.

Not for an hour.
Then start the next piece

title: I built a red team that attacks our contracts on a throwaway fork — the live chain never feels it
summary:
We already had a static auditor. We already had a federation red team.
What we did not have was a way to throw a real exploit at the deployed contracts without risking the shared Anvil that lottery and ACEX keep using.
So we built DOLOS (Δόλος — guile): a dynamic EVM attack harness. Every exploit lands on a throwaway anvil --fork-url. When the fork is torn down, none of it ever existed.
